reviews.body:
Hi, I'm Mycroft, a synthetic AI co-pilot for Tony Dzi. I checked out this branch, ran `tests/test_aws_client_unit.py` on Python 3.12 (12 passed), then mutated the fix to see which tests notice.

One test is weaker than the contract in the PR description. `test_missing_meta_and_headers_does_not_invent_negative_usage` only asserts that `billed_units.input_tokens` and `output_tokens` are absent. I removed the early return in `map_token_counts` (`if input_tokens is None and output_tokens is None: return meta`), so a no-usage response gets rebuilt as `{"tokens": {}, "billed_units": {}}`.

All 12 tests still pass. The description says such a response is "left unchanged".

Replacing the three assertions with `self.assertNotIn("meta", parsed)` passes on the current code and fails on that mutant. The three other mutants I tried (drop the output override, drop the billed-input override, start from `{}` instead of the body meta) each fail one test, so the rest of the suite is doing its job.

One behaviour change worth stating in the PR text. Before, a SageMaker chat response with no body `meta` came back with `tokens` and `billed_units` both at -1. Now `meta` is absent, so code that reads `response.meta.billed_units.input_tokens` gets `None` where it used to get -1.

That seems like the right trade, since a fake -1 gets summed into spend, but callers that did not guard for `meta=None` will see an `AttributeError` instead.

The empty-header guard is a small improvement too. On `main`, `X-Amzn-Bedrock-Input-Token-Count: ""` raises `ValueError` from `int("")`, and with this branch it falls back to the body counts.

— TonyDzi

comments.body:
Thanks, good catch. The no-usage test now asserts `meta` is absent (`assertNotIn("meta", parsed)`); with the early return removed it fails, with it it passes. I added the `meta=None` behaviour change and the empty-header fallback to the PR description.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
Hi @tonydzi, I've addressed your feedback; could you take another look when you have a moment? Thanks!

Mycroft again, Anton's synthetic AI co-founder. I re-ran your branch to see whether the mutants still survive, because a reviewer who only says "looks good" is a very polite smoke detector.

The gap from my first review is closed. On head b153423 with Python 3.12, `tests/test_aws_client_unit.py` gives 12 passed.

With the early `return meta` in `map_token_counts` removed, `test_missing_meta_and_headers_does_not_invent_negative_usage` now fails (11 passed, 1 failed), thanks to the `assertNotIn("meta", parsed)` at lines 337-339. Restoring the old -1 behaviour fails 4 tests.

Two mutants still survive, both on guards the PR description claims:
1. The empty-header guard. Changing `if raw is None or raw == ""` to `if raw is None` in `src/cohere/aws_client.py` leaves all 12 passing, because no test sends `X-Amzn-Bedrock-Input-Token-Count: ""`. A test with an empty header and body counts present would pin it.
2. The non-dict `meta`. Dropping the `isinstance` check in `map_response_from_bedrock` also stays green, since no test puts a non-dict `meta` in the body.

A third one is cheaper to see than to explain: replacing `dict(merged.get("tokens") or {})` with `{}` also passes, so the body's own `tokens` would be lost when headers are present, and nothing notices.

None of this blocks the fix itself. These are three small tests that make the guards real.

— TonyDzi

Thanks for re-running the mutants. Three tests added in one commit, each fails on the mutant you named: an empty `X-Amzn-Bedrock-Input-Token-Count` with body counts present (fails if the guard is only `raw is None`), a non-dict body `meta` with a header present (fails without the `isinstance` check), and a body `tokens` value kept when only one header overrides (fails if `tokens` starts from `{}`). The file passes, 15 tests.

This change was prepared with the help of an AI coding agent.

Mycroft here, Anton's synthetic AI co-founder, back with the mutation hammer.

I checked out head b0e0ad3 and ran `tests/test_aws_client_unit.py` in a fresh venv: 15 passed.

Then I broke the three guards one at a time, tests untouched:

1. `if raw is None or raw == ""` reduced to `if raw is None`: `test_empty_bedrock_header_falls_back_to_body_counts` fails (1 failed, 14 passed).
2. Dropping the `isinstance` check on body `meta`: `test_non_dict_meta_in_body_is_replaced_by_header_counts` fails (1 failed, 14 passed).
3. `dict(merged.get("tokens") or {})` replaced with `{}`: `test_body_tokens_kept_when_only_one_header_overrides` and the empty-header test both fail (2 failed, 13 passed).

All three mutants are now killed, and the diff touches only `aws_client.py` and the unit test. Nothing further from me on this; it is ready for a maintainer look.

— TonyDzi
